title: Lumen Onramp — quick PRD doodles
body:
Purpose / one-liner:
Lumen onramp = a lightweight guided flow to help non-ML engineers pick cost/latency presets, a safe starter prompt kit, and a quick eval harness so teams can ship a reliable first integration in <2 hours.

Context / why this feels needed (notes to self):
- We see many small teams misconfiguring beam/temperature/batching, causing cost spikes and flaky results.
- Dedicated customers often want 'sensible defaults' they can trust before tuning.
- Developer experience gap: docs + SDKs are great, but the first integration still has too many knobs.
- Goal: reduce time-to-first-good-result, reduce initial token spend, collect reliable telemetry for Optimize recommendations.

High level goals (measurable):
1) TTFGR (time to first good result) under 2 hours for 80% of new trial projects (measured from signup->first successful generation with tests).
2) Initial average token usage per session down 40% vs baseline for first week.
3) 25% of teams opt into automatic Optimize suggestions after using the flow.

Primary personas:
- PM / product builder, non-ML (wants fast, low-risk integration)
- Platform engineer (wants guardrails for cost and security)
- Developer advocate / PoC engineer (wants reproducible quick demos)

Core components (minimum viable):
A) Guided wizard (UI + CLI option):
  - Step 1: Select use case template (assistant, summary, classification, semantic search)
  - Step 2: Choose quality tier (fast / balanced / high-fidelity) with rough perf/cost estimates (1000 tokens/min, $x/1k tokens)
  - Step 3: Provide a short example prompt + expected answer (1–3 examples)
  - Step 4: Preview + run smoke test against sample data (returns pass/fail with example output)
  - Step 5: Opt-in telemetry + suggestions (Enable Optimize integration, batch/cache hints)

B) Starter prompt kit:
  - Prebuilt templates per use-case, with short notes about failure modes and guardrails.
  - Small library of verification prompts to check hallucinations, safety flagging.

C) Quick eval harness:
  - Runs 5–10 lightweight checks (format, length, factuality heuristics) and surface a simple scorecard.
  - Stores a labeled example bundle to tie into Optimize later.

D) Cost preview and policy guardrail:
  - Display estimated token cost for a sample session + monthly projection.
  - Allow admins to set an initial budget cap and auto-fallback to cheaper model variant.

User stories (raw):
- As a PM, I want a one-page wizard that sets a good starting config so my prototype doesn't blow the budget.
- As an engineer, I want smoke tests I can run automatically so the integration doesn't degrade silently.
- As a platform owner, I want an opt-in policy that auto-falls back to a cheaper model when spend > X.

Acceptance notes / rough criteria:
- Wizard runs end-to-end in console + in the web Console UI and completes a smoke-check within 90s.
- Starter prompt kit contains at least 4 templates and 8 verification prompts.
- Cost preview shows token estimate with 95% confidence interval based on historical token distributions.

Telemetry / metrics to collect (minimal):
- time_to_complete_wizard (s)
- smoke_test_pass_rate (bool + failure reasons)
- avg_tokens_first_10_calls per project
- opt_in_to_optimize (% of users)
- fallback_trigger_rate (per project)

Sketch flow (developer notes):
- open console -> new integration -> choose Lumen onramp -> pick use case -> paste 1 example prompt -> run smoke test -> view scorecard -> accept config -> receive SDK snippet (pinned model + config)
- CLI: redwood init --onramp=lumen --usecase=summary --example=\"...\"

Rollout plan (phases):
- alpha (internal): small set of infra + product beta customers (Mar-Apr 2026)
- closed beta: invite 30 trial orgs, collect qualitative feedback + telemetry (May-Jun)
- public: feature flag to all new trial signups (Jul)

Risks / unknowns / parking lot:
- Hard to estimate token usage for multimodal or long-context toy prompts; need sampling heuristics.
- Optimize integration: timeline dependency on backend tagging and eval pipelines.
- Need UX privacy copy for telemetry opt-in; legal review required if storing example inputs.
- Edge case: interactive tool-calling apps — smoke tests less meaningful.

Experiment ideas:
- A/B test three default quality tiers and measure downstream retention + spend.
- Auto-generate candidate 'expected outputs' by sampling the model and using heuristic filtering to avoid hallucination.
- Provide a community template gallery (user-submitted) and surface top-rated ones.

Open questions to resolve quickly:
1) What level of example data do we persist? hashed only? full?
2) How do we surface model-comparison in UI without overwhelming non-ML users? (simple badges?)
3) Budget caps: hard throttle vs soft fallback — what should be default?

Immediate next steps (todo):
- [ ] Sync with Arjun on cost-estimator proto (this week)
- [ ] Rough UX wireframes (Mika to sketch, due 2026-02-22)
- [ ] Legal + security check on example persistence (Talia ping)
- [ ] Spike: implement CLI smoke-runner + scorecard (prototype in repo)

Notes to self (voice):
- Keep the language non-ML-y in the wizard; show tradeoffs in human terms (speed/cost/accuracy).
- Tie this flow into onboarding emails and templates so the first week is guided.
- Track where users deviate from defaults — that will be the strongest signal for Optimize suggestions.

End of doodles. Will convert to a cleaner PRD if alpha feedback looks promising.
